pages.title: Docs home
pages.summary: GitVault documentation home and common tasks.
pages.keywords: documentation overview home common tasks
pages.excerpt: Start from GitVault documentation home to find setup, sync, devices, recovery, and troubleshooting pages.

pages.title: Quick start
pages.summary: Create your vault, save recovery, set a PIN, add an item, and connect encrypted sync.
pages.keywords: setup onboarding create vault recovery phrase pin github sync first run link device restore
pages.excerpt: Start with a new vault, write down the recovery phrase, set a 4-6 digit PIN, add one vault item, then connect GitHub sync if you need backup or more devices.

pages.title: GitHub sync setup
pages.summary: Prepare a private repository and fine-grained token for encrypted GitVault storage.
pages.keywords: github repository repo token pat fine grained contents metadata private sync storage bearer classic token
pages.excerpt: GitHub is only encrypted storage. GitVault encrypts locally, writes ciphertext files to one private repository, and needs a fine-grained token with minimal repository permissions.

pages.title: Platform support
pages.summary: Feature availability across web, Android, Windows, macOS, and Linux.
pages.keywords: platform support web android desktop windows macos linux browser apk autofill keyboard biometric ssh terminal mcp ai apps
pages.excerpt: Core vault features work across web, Android, and Desktop. Android adds system integrations; Desktop adds local MCP access for approved AI apps.

pages.title: Sync behavior
pages.summary: How encrypted GitHub sync, auto-sync, conflict handling, deletion tombstones, and device checks work.
pages.keywords: sync behavior auto sync last write wins conflict tombstones deleted items interval github device revocation
pages.excerpt: GitVault syncs encrypted vault data and trust records through GitHub. Auto-sync can run in the background, conflicts resolve by latest change, and deletes are retained as tombstones.

pages.title: Passwords
pages.summary: Add, group, search, copy, edit, delete, and fill password entries.
pages.keywords: password credentials username url notes group dropdown create group copy edit delete autofill totp
pages.excerpt: Password entries store login title, username, password, URL, notes, group, and optional TOTP data. Groups can be selected or created from the same dropdown.

pages.title: Notes
pages.summary: Write encrypted Markdown notes with linked knowledge, daily journals, templates, tasks, and import or export.
pages.keywords: notes markdown wiki links backlinks blocks graph daily journal templates tasks import export aliases tags archive search
pages.excerpt: Notes use canonical Markdown with preview, task progress, wiki links, aliases, backlinks, block references, daily journals, encrypted templates, and a local knowledge graph.

pages.title: AI Apps and MCP
pages.summary: Connect MCP-compatible AI applications to approved GitVault notes with per-app permissions.
pages.keywords: ai apps mcp model context protocol desktop windows macos linux stdio streamable http permissions tags approval revoke rotate credential tray
pages.excerpt: GitVault Desktop hosts a local MCP service for notes. Every AI app gets its own credential, permissions, tag scope, write policy, and redacted activity history.

pages.title: 2FA codes
pages.summary: Store TOTP secrets, organize codes by group, copy live codes, and handle countdown timing.
pages.keywords: 2fa totp authenticator code timer secret issuer account group dropdown copy countdown
pages.excerpt: GitVault works as an authenticator for TOTP secrets. Codes regenerate on the normal timer and can be copied from the 2FA page or password details.

pages.title: TOTP import
pages.summary: Import authenticator secrets from manual secrets, otpauth links, or QR codes when supported.
pages.keywords: totp import otpauth qr code scanner secret google authenticator issuer account migration
pages.excerpt: GitVault accepts manual TOTP secrets and otpauth links. QR scanning depends on camera support; paste the link or secret when scanning is unavailable.

pages.title: SSH credentials
pages.summary: Save SSH hosts, ports, usernames, passwords, keys, and Android terminal entries.
pages.keywords: ssh terminal host username port password private key android credentials ping connect session
pages.excerpt: SSH entries store host credentials in the encrypted vault. Android can open terminal workflows where supported by the build and device.

pages.title: Autofill and GitVault Keyboard
pages.summary: Enable Android autofill and GitVault Keyboard for easier password entry in other apps.
pages.keywords: android autofill service keyboard ime inline suggestions samsung chrome pixel gboard swiftkey
headings: Enable autofill on Pixel or stock Android
pages.excerpt: Android autofill works after selecting GitVault as the system autofill service. GitVault Keyboard is the fallback for apps or browsers that do not expose fields correctly.

pages.title: Security model
pages.summary: How local encryption, unlock, biometric, duress mode, clipboard clearing, storage, and trust work.
pages.keywords: security encryption xchacha20 poly1305 local first pin biometric lock auth interval duress panic clipboard github ciphertext
pages.excerpt: GitVault encrypts data locally with authenticated encryption before GitHub sync. Local unlock is protected by PIN and optional biometric support, with duress and clipboard safety settings.

pages.title: Settings
pages.summary: Configuration reference for PIN, biometric, auth interval, sync, clipboard, autofill, keyboard, theme, devices, and recovery.
pages.keywords: settings theme clipboard autofill keyboard github biometric pin interval recovery kit connected devices auto sync lock
pages.excerpt: Settings controls unlock behavior, biometric unlock, authentication interval, clipboard clearing, GitHub sync, auto-sync, autofill, keyboard, devices, and recovery kit access.

pages.title: Connected devices
pages.summary: Link, approve, recognize, remove, and recover trusted web and Android devices.
pages.keywords: devices linked trusted remove approval recognize recovery token registry alert link new device qr transfer code pin
headings: Device added outside Link New Device
pages.excerpt: Connected Devices shows trusted web and Android devices after they link or restore and sync. Removing a device makes it untrusted, and it must link or restore again.

pages.title: Recovery flows
pages.summary: Restore with trusted-device approval or recover after losing every trusted device with old and new GitHub tokens.
pages.keywords: recovery phrase trusted device approval old token new token lost all devices restore onboarding wait approval
headings: Restore after losing every trusted device
pages.excerpt: Recovery starts with the normal trusted-device approval path. If no trusted device can answer, use recovery phrase plus old GitHub access and a newly generated GitHub token.

pages.title: Install and update
pages.summary: Open the web app, install Android APKs or Desktop archives, verify release assets, and understand version updates.
pages.keywords: install update apk universal abi desktop windows macos linux archive zip tar sha256 release tag github pages web app version android
pages.excerpt: The web app is served at /app/, while Android and Desktop builds are published on GitHub Releases. Their visible version is derived from the release tag.

pages.title: Release verification
pages.summary: Verify APK and Desktop archive checksums plus the deployed web version before trusting an update.
pages.keywords: release verification apk desktop windows macos linux archive zip tar sha256 checksum sha256sums version tag github releases web pages verify download
pages.excerpt: Use the matching SHA256SUMS file from the same GitHub release to verify an Android or Desktop download, then check the in-app version against the release tag.

pages.title: FAQ and common mistakes
pages.summary: Answers for common setup, sync, device trust, recovery, autofill, and release questions.
pages.keywords: faq common mistakes github token device alert recognize link device restore recovery autofill checksum web version pin throttling
pages.excerpt: Common GitVault mistakes include using the wrong token permission, skipping the recovery phrase, recognizing an unknown device too quickly, and expecting Android autofill before selecting GitVault as provider.

pages.title: Troubleshooting
pages.summary: Diagnose sync, token, unlock, device, autofill, biometric, web version, and Android issues in order.
pages.keywords: troubleshooting sync token device pin biometric autofill alert web android version github pages diagnostics
pages.excerpt: Start with unlock and internet, then check repository and token permissions, source-device sync, target-device sync, device trust, and platform-specific settings.
